flows.name: Visit landing page
flows.goal: Understand what NeonBoard is for and get started.

steps.userAction: The visitor opens the NeonBoard landing page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that NeonBoard is for building personal dashboards with notes, counters, checklists and link lists, and invites the visitor to sign up or sign in to create a dashboard.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-up form.

alternatives.condition: The visitor chooses to sign in instead.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-in form.

flows.outcome: Nothing is changed; the visitor knows how to sign up or sign in.

flows.name: Sign up
flows.goal: Create an account and be signed in.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty account form.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the account form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the account, signs the member in, and shows the dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: The email or password is missing or invalid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The new member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty dashboard list and offers Create as the next action.

flows.outcome: The account is created and the member is signed in; it stays that way after a refresh.

flows.name: Sign in
flows.goal: Sign in to reach my dashboards.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty account form.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the account form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website signs the member in and shows the dashboard list with when each dashboard was last edited.

alternatives.condition: The email or password is missing or invalid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty dashboard list and offers Create as the next action.

flows.outcome: The member is signed in and stays signed in after a refresh.

flows.name: Sign out

steps.userAction: The member chooses to sign out.
steps.websiteResponse: The website ends the session and shows the public landing page.

flows.outcome: The member is signed out and stays signed out after a refresh.

flows.name: Create a dashboard
flows.goal: Start a new dashboard and land in its editor.

steps.userAction: The member chooses Create.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates a dashboard named Untitled dashboard, saves it automatically, and opens its empty editor offering adding a widget as the next action.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the dashboard list as it was and offers to retry Create.

flows.outcome: A new dashboard named Untitled dashboard exists and its empty editor is shown; it is still there after a refresh.

flows.name: View dashboard list
flows.goal: Find and reopen one of my dashboards.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all of the member's own dashboards ordered by when each was last edited, most recently edited first, with that time.

steps.userAction: The member chooses one dashboard from the list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website opens that dashboard in the editor and shows its widgets.

alternatives.condition: The member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no dashboards yet and offers Create as the next action.

alternatives.condition: The chosen dashboard was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: The opened dashboard has no widgets yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the empty dashboard editor and offers adding a widget as the next action.

flows.outcome: No data is changed; the chosen dashboard is open in the editor and is still open after a refresh.

flows.name: Add a widget
flows.goal: Add a note, counter, checklist or link list widget to the dashboard.
preconditions: At least one dashboard, opened in the editor.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to add a widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the widget type choices of note, counter, checklist and link list.

steps.userAction: The member chooses a widget type.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the widget with a default title based on its type, medium size and empty or zero settings at the end of the dashboard order, saves it automatically, and shows it on the dashboard with an updated last-edited time.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks that a type must be chosen and keeps the type choices shown.
The website keeps the type choice and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The member cancels adding a widget.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is added; the website shows the dashboard as it was.

flows.outcome: A new widget of the chosen type is on the dashboard and is still there after a refresh.

flows.name: Use a note widget
flows.goal: Keep plain text in a note widget.
preconditions: A dashboard with a note widget.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard in the editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard with its widgets including the note widget with its title and plain text.

steps.userAction: The member edits the note widget title.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new title automatically and shows the updated title with an updated last-edited time.

steps.userAction: The member edits the note text.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new text automatically and shows the updated note.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the empty dashboard editor and offers adding a widget as the next action.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard belongs to another member.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website does not show the dashboard and shows the member's own dashboard list.
The website marks the title and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed title and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The note text is longer than 5000 characters.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the text and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed text and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: The note title and text are updated and are still there after a refresh.

flows.name: Use a counter widget
flows.goal: Track a number with a counter widget.
preconditions: A dashboard with a counter widget.

steps.userAction: The member opens a dashboard with a counter widget in the editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name and its widgets in order; the counter widget shows its title, label and number with controls to increase and decrease.

steps.userAction: The member edits the counter title and label.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves each change automatically, shows the updated title and label, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

steps.userAction: The member increases or decreases the counter number.
steps.websiteResponse: The website changes the number by 1, saves it automatically, shows the updated number, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard or its counter widget was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard or widget is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website marks the title as required and keeps what was typed.

alternatives.condition: Saving the title or label fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.
The website keeps the previous number and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: The counter title, label and number are updated and are still there after a refresh.

flows.name: Use a checklist widget
flows.goal: Track tasks in a checklist widget.
preconditions: A dashboard with a checklist widget.

steps.userAction: The member opens a dashboard with a checklist widget in the editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name and its widgets in order; the checklist widget shows its title and its items with ticked or unticked states.

steps.userAction: The member edits the checklist title.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new title automatically, shows the updated title, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

steps.userAction: The member adds a new checklist item with text.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the item as unticked automatically, shows it at the end of the checklist, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

steps.userAction: The member ticks or unticks a checklist item.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new ticked state automatically, shows the updated state, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

alternatives.condition: The checklist widget has no items yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the checklist widget with no items and offers adding an item as the next action.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard or its checklist widget was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard or widget is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website marks the title as required and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed value and offers to retry.
The website marks the item text as required and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed value and offers to retry.
The website keeps the previous ticked state and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: The checklist title, items and ticked states are updated and are still there after a refresh.

flows.name: Use a link list widget
flows.goal: Keep and open useful links in a link list widget.
preconditions: A dashboard with a link list widget.

steps.userAction: The member opens a dashboard with a link list widget in the editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name and its widgets in order; the link list widget shows its title and its entries with titles and web addresses.

steps.userAction: The member edits the link list title.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new title automatically, shows the updated title, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

steps.userAction: The member adds a link entry with a title and a web address.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the entry automatically, shows it in the link list, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

steps.userAction: The member chooses a link in the widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website opens the link web address for the member and keeps the link list unchanged.

alternatives.condition: The link list widget has no entries yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the link list widget with no entries and offers adding a link as the next action.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard or its link list widget was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard or widget is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website marks the title as required and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed value and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The link title is empty or the web address is missing or not a valid web address.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The chosen link was removed in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the link is gone and shows the updated link list.

flows.outcome: The link list title and entries are updated and are still there after a refresh; choosing a link opens its address.

flows.name: Move and resize a widget
flows.goal: Arrange widgets by position and size.
preconditions: A dashboard with at least one widget.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard in the editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name and its widgets in their relative order with their sizes.

steps.userAction: The member changes a widget position relative to the other widgets.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new order automatically, shows the widgets rearranged, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

steps.userAction: The member resizes the widget between small, medium and large.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new size automatically, shows the widget with its new size, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

alternatives.condition: There are no widgets on the dashboard.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the empty dashboard and offers adding a widget as the next action.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website keeps the previous order and offers to retry.
The website marks the size as required and keeps the current size.
The website keeps the previous size and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: The widget order and size are updated and are still there after a refresh.

flows.name: Remove a widget
flows.goal: Remove a widget I no longer want.
preconditions: A dashboard with at least one widget.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard in the editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name and its widgets in order.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to remove the widget.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard or widget was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard or widget is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website shows the dashboard without the removed widget and with the remaining widgets in their existing order.
Nothing is removed; the website shows the dashboard with the widget unchanged.

flows.outcome: The widget is gone and stays gone after a refresh; other widgets keep their order.

flows.name: Rename a dashboard
flows.goal: Give a dashboard a meaningful name.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard in the editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name and its widgets.

steps.userAction: The member renames the dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new name automatically, shows it in the editor and in the dashboard list, and updates when the dashboard was last edited.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website marks the name as required and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed value and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: The dashboard has its new name and it is still there after a refresh.

flows.name: Duplicate a dashboard
flows.goal: Copy a dashboard to reuse its setup.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all of the member's own dashboards ordered by when each was last edited with that time.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to duplicate a dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates a new dashboard named with copy added to the original name with copies of all widgets, titles, type settings, positions and sizes, and shows it in the list and in the editor.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows no dashboards and offers Create as the next action.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.
The website keeps the dashboard list unchanged and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: A new dashboard copy exists alongside the original and both are still there after a refresh.

flows.name: Delete a dashboard
flows.goal: Delete a dashboard I no longer want.

steps.userAction: The member opens the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all of the member's own dashboards ordered by when each was last edited with that time.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to delete a dashboard.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows no dashboards and offers Create as the next action.
The website shows the dashboard list without the deleted dashboard and its widgets.
Nothing is deleted; the website shows the dashboard list unchanged.
The website says the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.

flows.outcome: The dashboard and its widgets are gone and stay gone after a refresh.

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Secret that proves ownership of the account

fields.label: Dashboard name
fields.meaning: How the member refers to the dashboard in the list and editor

fields.label: Widget type
fields.meaning: Which kind of widget to add to the dashboard

fields.label: Widget title
fields.meaning: How the member refers to the widget on the dashboard

fields.label: Widget size
fields.meaning: How large the widget appears among the other widgets

fields.label: Note text
fields.meaning: Plain text kept in a note widget

fields.label: Counter number
fields.meaning: Current count kept in a counter widget

fields.label: Checklist item text
fields.meaning: Text of one item inside a checklist widget

fields.label: Link title
fields.meaning: Readable name shown for a web address in a link list widget

fields.label: Link web address
fields.meaning: Web address opened when the member chooses the link

steps.websiteResponse: The website asks to confirm the deletion and says what else will be removed with it.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website deletes the record and what belongs to it.
Nothing is deleted; the record stays as it was.

assumptions.text: The dashboard list is ordered by last edited, most recently edited first, so the member can find recent work without search or filters.

Dashboard name and widget title are required and cannot be saved empty; Create uses 'Untitled dashboard' and adding a widget uses a default title based on its type, and clearing a name in the editor is rejected.
